title: The Fox and the Grapes: exercises
subtitle: Five exercises on the text
label: Exercises
review: Written by Claude from the lesson text. Check the English and the answers before using it with learners.

items.q: The fox was hot and hungry.
The fox stretched his paws as high as he could.
After many tries, the fox was tired.

items.why: “One sunny afternoon, a fox was walking through the countryside.”

items.q: What were the grapes hanging from?
items.why: “Then he saw something hanging from a vine.”

items.q: What did the fox do after he stepped back?
options: He ran toward the vine and jumped again
items.why: “He stepped back and ran toward the vine. Then he jumped again.”

items.q: What did the fox say about the grapes at the end?
Why did the fox say the grapes were sour?
options: Because he could not reach them
items.why: “The fox only said that because he could not reach them.”

items.before: But the grapes were still out of

items.after: we do not want something when we cannot have it.

blocks.title: 4. Open questions
blocks.note: These questions are open. Talk about your answers with your teacher or a classmate.

items.q: Without looking at the text, sum it up in three sentences.
items.model: A hot and hungry fox saw a bunch of grapes hanging high on a vine. He jumped again and again, but he could not reach them. So he walked away and said the grapes were probably sour.

items.q: What did the grapes look like?
items.model: They were purple, and they looked sweet and juicy.

items.q: How did the fox try to get the grapes?
items.model: He jumped and stretched his paws as high as he could. He stepped back, ran toward the vine and jumped again and again.

items.q: Were the grapes really sour? Why did the fox say they were?
items.model: No, they were not sour. He only said that because he could not reach them.

items.q: Have you ever said you didn't want something because you couldn't have it?

blocks.title: 5. Put in order
blocks.intro: Put the events in the order of the story.
items: The fox saw a bunch of purple grapes
The fox jumped and stretched his paws
He stepped back and ran toward the vine
The fox turned around and walked away
